originalRequest: fix the ui make it look professional looking , make it responseive for mobile , fix the color theme and push it after verifying everything
subject: Job Tracker: a personal job application tracking web app (React/Vite frontend, Spring Boot backend) that lists scraped and manually added jobs, tracks status, handles referrals, and runs ATS scoring and resume tailoring
scope: Restyle the whole existing frontend (frontend/src/styles.css and components) so it looks professional, works on mobile, and uses a fixed, coherent color theme. Existing features, data flow and API calls stay as they are.
primaryGoal: Let the user scan, filter and act on job applications quickly with a clean, trustworthy interface on desktop and mobile
audience: The app owner (a software engineer job hunting) using it daily on a laptop and on a phone
offer: One workspace for tracking jobs from multiple sources (LinkedIn, Workday, Naukri, Instahyre, manual), with status tracking, referral notes, ATS scoring and Claude resume tailoring
primaryAction: Select a job to open its details, then update its status or tailor the resume; secondary actions are Add Job and Sync
creativeControl: Delegated: the designer may refine or replace the color palette and spacing, typography scale and component styling for a professional look, keeping it a focused productivity tool rather than a marketing page
requiredContent: Login screen: sign-in form for the single user, centered and readable on mobile
Header: app title, Sync button with live label, Resume button, Logout, collapsing cleanly on small screens
Toolbar: source tabs (auto/manual etc.), status filter, search input, sort select, needs-referral toggle, Add Job button; wraps or scrolls horizontally on mobile
Job list: job cards grouped by day with company, title, location, source, status badge and tailoring-in-progress state, plus Load more pagination and loading/empty states

Detail panel: selected job's full info, status controls, edit/delete, ATS score card and ATS section, referral section, tailor section; side panel on desktop, full-screen sheet with back control on mobile
Job form modal: add/edit job fields, usable as full-screen on mobile
Resume modal and PDF preview modal: resume management and tailored PDF preview with download, sized for mobile viewports
constraints: Keep all existing React behavior, state, API calls and component structure; styling-focused changes
Responsive from 360px phones to wide desktops, touch targets at least 44px on mobile
Accessible contrast for text and status badges in the chosen theme
After changes, verify with a production build (vite build) and a visual check, then commit and push to master
Do not commit unrelated pending changes to resume.tex, resume.pdf, resume.log
brandInputs: Existing theme (frontend/src/styles.css :root): dark color-scheme, bg #0e1015, surface #171a22/#1d212b, border #272c38, text #e8eaf1/#a3a8ba/#70768a, accent indigo #6d66f2, status colors success #34d399, warning #fbbf24, danger #f87171, info #60a5fa
Existing typography: Inter with system sans fallback
Existing radii 8/12/16px and shadow tokens; no logo found
assumptions: 'Fix the color theme' means replacing the current palette with a more restrained, consistent token set; dark theme kept as the base unless the new palette clearly reads better
Treated as a dashboard (operating product UI), so no marketing sections or eight-section minimum
Useful transitions included for tabs, filters, detail panel open/close, modals and list loading; no decorative scroll animation
Only 6 media queries exist today, so mobile layout needs a real master-detail pattern rather than tweaks
Push goes to the existing master branch with only frontend changes staged
unresolved: Whether the user wants a light-mode option as well; default is a single polished dark theme
